issues.description: The problem statement's UML and text specify calculateTotalPrice(Meal) should return a double (for financial precision), but the solution implements calculateTotalPrice as a static method returning int. This return-type mismatch is structural: students will be expected to implement a method returning double per the specification, but the provided reference returns int, and tests may expect double precision.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent. Either change the problem statement/UML to expect an int (if integer sums are intended) or (preferable) change the implementation of calculateTotalPrice to return double and perform summation using double precision. Update any related tests and documentation to match the chosen type.

issues.description: The problem text instructs that both attributes (orders and stock) should be initialized in the constructor, but elsewhere (later note) explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). Initializing a static stock in an instance constructor contradicts the later requirement that stock be static/final. The solution declares stock as a static final field initialized at declaration. This inconsistency in the problem statement about where/how to initialize stock can confuse students.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement: specify that orders is an instance (non-static) field initialized in the constructor, while stock is a static (and optionally final) field shared across all instances and should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. Remove or reword the sentence that suggests initializing stock in the instance constructor.
